ops.body:
Recurred on CI, and this time it failed a release.

`test (macos-latest)` on `a34f8b9` (the `chore(release): sync ccx.binrun + manifest to v0.57.0` commit), CI run 33782135054:

    --- FAIL: TestRestackGTPerBranchVerdict (25.42s)
        --- FAIL: TestRestackGTPerBranchVerdict/the_stack_landed_on_trunk (6.35s)
            testing.go:1464: TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat /var/folders/.../TestRestackGTPerBranchVerdictthe_stack_landed_on_trunk20418968/001: directory not empty

No assertion in the subtest body failed — the body passed and only the deferred `t.TempDir()` cleanup errored, consistent with a gt/jj subprocess still holding a handle in the temp working tree when `RemoveAll` runs.

What makes this worth more than a re-run: it propagated. `release.yml`'s `descriptor` job ends by dispatching `ci.yml`/`guides.yml` against the freshly-committed descriptor and waiting on them, so this flake turned the whole v0.57.0 release run red — after `release`, `publish-tap`, `smoke`, and descriptor's own commit and upload steps had all succeeded. The release was functionally complete and the tap formula published; only the workflow's success bit was wrong. Anyone reading `gh run list` would reasonably conclude the release had failed.

So the cost of this flake is no longer one re-run: it is a red release run that has to be triaged before anyone can tell whether a published release is sound. Recovery was `gh run rerun <ci-run> --failed` on the dispatched run only — re-running the `descriptor` job itself risks re-attempting its already-succeeded commit-to-main step.

Argues for raising priority, and for the fix being in the test's cleanup ordering (wait for or kill the spawned gt/jj processes before the temp dir is reclaimed) rather than a retry wrapper.

Observed 2026-09-03, macos-latest runner, `-race`.
